sources.ref: FP Infographic Studio / Patrick works 28:3 — Template WhiteH:1080px 28:92 and 28:177, and the six #E5E5E5 works

color.neutral.note: the dark ramp mirrored by rank, so every step keeps a measured brand grey and the ends trade places; 100 = #151618 (Template WhiteH:1080px 28:176 title fill); 150 = #191919 (Template WhiteH:1080px 28:174 title fill); 780 = #CCCECE (Background Image 28:94 decoration gradient, last stop); 790 = #D4D4D4 (FP logo 28:98 watermark gradient, last stop); 910 = #DFDFDF (FP logo 28:98 watermark gradient, first stop); 1000 = #E5E5E5 (Template WhiteH:1080px 28:92 frame fill)

color.accent.note: hue and saturation are the dark pack's measured hues; lightness is lowered only until the colour clears 3:1 against the paper, which is the floor WCAG sets for a graphical object. The light works use no consistent accent vocabulary - #4E81EE, #E28F62, #5470C6, #F2A01E, #1A3487 and #5C9BD6 appear across six frames - so there was nothing to measure

canvas.overlay.note: the light template 28:92 and all six light works are a flat fill plus the corner blobs: no edge gradient. The dark overlay is measured from published report frames, and mirroring it puts a grey wash over paper, so the light pack deletes it rather than inventing a pale one

chrome.decoration.fill.note: Background Image 28:94: the corner blobs run from paper white, so the light pack points the first stop at neutral.1050 instead of neutral.0, which is ink here
